solution.title: Parity constraints determine the final row and column
steps: Choose the entries in the first three rows and first three columns freely. There are 3 × 3 = 9 independent binary entries.
For each of the first three rows, the even-parity requirement fixes its fourth entry.
For each of the first three columns, the even-parity requirement fixes the entry in the fourth row.
The bottom-right entry is then consistent with both the last-row and last-column parity constraints.
Therefore the number of matrices is 2^9 = 512.
solution.note: Original editorial explanation based on the official question and final key.

solution.title: Match each addressing mode to how the operand is specified
steps: Immediate addressing embeds a constant directly in the instruction.
Indirect addressing obtains the operand through an address held in a pointer or address location.
Base-with-index addressing naturally selects an array element using a base and index.
Base-with-displacement addressing accesses a field at a fixed offset from a base, such as a record field.
The matching is P–4, Q–2, R–1, S–3.
solution.note: Original editorial explanation based on the official question and final key.

solution.title: Read-after-write is the classic data dependency hazard
steps: A read-after-write (RAW) dependency occurs when a later instruction needs a value produced by an earlier instruction.
If the later instruction reads before the earlier instruction has written or forwarded the result, it may consume a stale value.
That is why a pipeline may need forwarding, a stall, or hazard detection logic.
Read-after-read does not create a write/read dependency.
solution.note: Original editorial explanation based on the official question and final key.

solution.title: TCP endpoints can initiate connection close independently
steps: TCP is full-duplex, so each endpoint has its own sending direction to close.
Either endpoint may send a FIN first; the other endpoint can later send its own FIN.
Both sides can also initiate close at nearly the same time, producing a simultaneous-close sequence.
Therefore simultaneous initiation is allowed by TCP.

solution.title: A non-zero null-space vector forces the determinant to be zero
steps: If a non-zero vector x satisfies Mx = 0, then M has a non-trivial null space.
A square matrix with a non-trivial null space is singular, so its determinant is zero.
The null space contains every scalar multiple of x, including at least two distinct non-zero vectors.
The rank is not necessarily one.
solution.note: Original editorial explanation based on the official question and final key.

solution.title: Leaf positions in a 1-indexed binary min-heap
steps: In a 1-indexed array representation, the children of node i are at indices 2i and 2i + 1.
Therefore, an index i is an internal node when 2i ≤ n, which is equivalent to i ≤ floor(n/2).
All indices greater than floor(n/2) are leaves. Since n is odd, the first leaf index is (n + 1)/2.
Thus (n − 1)/2 and (n − 3)/2 are internal-node indices, not leaves. The correct selections are B and C.
solution.note: Original worked explanation cross-checked against the official final answer key.

solution.title: Apply linear probing in insertion order
steps: Compute the home slot h(x) = (x + 7) mod 11 for each key and insert in the given order.
The keys 1, 13, 22 and 15 occupy slots 8, 9, 7 and 0 respectively.
For key 11, the home slot is 7; slots 7, 8 and 9 are occupied, so linear probing places 11 in slot 10.
For key 24, the home slot is 9; slots 9, 10 and 0 are occupied, so it is placed in slot 1.
Slot 2 remains empty, matching option C.
solution.note: Original worked explanation cross-checked against the official final answer key.
